title: Choice: the logit
summary: GCAM never gives the whole market to the cheapest option. A logit shares it out by relative cost, with share weights calibrated to history. Learn the formula, the exponent and nesting.
outcomes: You can compute logit shares for three technologies by hand
You can explain what the logit exponent and share weights do
You can tell the relative-cost and absolute-cost logit apart
You can describe GCAM's nested choice from sector to technology
narration_en: If coal costs sixty dollars, gas seventy and solar eighty, a simple model would build only coal. Real investors do not behave like that. Sites differ, preferences differ, costs vary from place to place, so cheaper options win more of the market but not all of it. GCAM captures this with the logit, a formula that turns costs into market shares. Each option's cost is raised to a negative power, called the logit exponent, and divided by the sum over all options. A small exponent spreads the market widely. A large exponent behaves almost like winner takes all. Share weights are extra numbers calibrated so that the base year reproduces the shares we actually observe; they carry everything the costs leave out. Choices are also nested: electricity first chooses between fuels, then between technologies within each fuel, then between cooling systems. In this module you will compute shares by hand, calibrate share weights, and build a two-level nest in code.
narration_ar: إذا كانت تكلفة الفحم ستين دولارًا والغاز سبعين والطاقة الشمسية ثمانين، فإن نموذجًا بسيطًا سيبني الفحم فقط. لكن المستثمرين الحقيقيين لا يتصرفون هكذا. فالمواقع تختلف والتفضيلات تختلف والتكاليف تتفاوت من مكان لآخر، لذلك يفوز الخيار الأرخص بحصة أكبر من السوق لكن ليس بكاملها. يلتقط نموذج GCAM ذلك بدالة اللوجيت، وهي صيغة تحوّل التكاليف إلى حصص سوقية. تُرفع تكلفة كل خيار إلى قوة سالبة تسمى أُس اللوجيت، وتُقسم على مجموع كل الخيارات. الأُس الصغير يوزع السوق توزيعًا واسعًا، والأُس الكبير يقترب من أن يأخذ الفائز كل شيء. أوزان الحصص أرقام إضافية تُعايَر بحيث تعيد سنة الأساس إنتاج الحصص المرصودة فعلًا، وهي تحمل كل ما لا تعبّر عنه التكاليف. والاختيارات متداخلة أيضًا: فالكهرباء تختار أولًا بين أنواع الوقود، ثم بين التقنيات داخل كل وقود، ثم بين أنظمة التبريد. في هذه الوحدة ستحسب الحصص يدويًا، وتعاير أوزان الحصص، وتبني تداخلًا من مستويين بالشيفرة.

diagram.title: Nested choice for electricity
diagram.caption: Each level of the tree has its own logit. Costs flow up the tree; shares flow down it.

nodes.label: Electricity sector
nodes.detail: The sector's output must meet demand. It splits its market among subsectors (fuels) with a logit; electricity subsector exponent in the reference example is −3 (choice.html).

nodes.label: Coal subsector
nodes.detail: Within coal, technologies compete with an aggressive exponent (−10 in the reference example): small cost differences swing shares a lot.

nodes.label: Gas subsector
nodes.detail: Gas plants (combined cycle, turbines, with or without CCS) share the gas subsector by their own logit.

nodes.label: Solar subsector
nodes.detail: Solar technologies; their effective cost includes a value-factor adjustment that rises with market share (Go 2.4).

nodes.label: Pulverised coal
nodes.detail: A technology: cost = non-energy cost + fuel cost + emissions cost (en_technologies.html).

nodes.label: Coal with CCS
nodes.detail: Higher non-energy cost, but much lower emissions cost under a carbon price.

nodes.label: Cooling system
nodes.detail: For thermal plants the last level chooses one of up to five cooling systems, by a cost logit that includes water prices (demand_water.html).

nodes.label: Share weights
nodes.detail: Share weights scale each option so base-year shares match history; they also phase in new technologies (choice.html).

tour.text: Electricity demand must be met. The sector does not pick one fuel: it shares the market.
First level: fuels compete by cost with a moderate exponent (−3 in the reference example).
Inside coal, technologies compete with a steep exponent (−10): close substitutes switch quickly.
Thermal plants then choose a cooling system, linking electricity to water prices.
Share weights calibrate each branch to 2021 data and phase new options in.

sections.heading: Why not cheapest-takes-all?
sections.html: A model that always picks the single cheapest technology flips its whole mix when costs cross, which real markets never do. Costs vary across sites and investors; some preferences are unmeasured. The logit turns costs into smooth market shares: cheaper wins more, never everything (choice.html).

sections.heading: The relative-cost logit
sections.html:
si = αi · ciγ / Σj αj · cjγ, γ < 0

With equal share weights and γ = −4, coal $60, gas $70, solar $80: 60−4 = 7.72×10−8, 70−4 = 4.16×10−8, 80−4 = 2.44×10−8. The sum is 14.32×10−8, so the shares are 54%, 29% and 17%. With γ = −1 they are 38/33/29%; with γ = −10, 79/17/4%.

sections.heading: The absolute-cost logit
sections.html:
si = αi · exp(β · ci) / Σj αj · exp(β · cj)

Here the share ratio depends on the cost difference rather than the ratio. GCAM users always enter a logit exponent; for the absolute form GCAM derives β from it. The absolute form behaves well when costs can be near zero or negative, and GCAM uses it in places such as direct air capture and the passenger transport nests (choice.html).

sections.heading: Share weights and calibration
sections.html: Share weights are set so that, at base-year costs, the logit reproduces the observed 2021 shares. If observed shares are 30/50/20% at costs 60/70/80 and γ = −4, then α ∝ share / cγ, giving weights 1 : 3.088 : 2.107 (normalised to coal). They also phase in new technologies: low in their first year, rising toward a neutral value. Future share weights are assumptions, so treat them as a scenario lever, not a fact.

sections.heading: Nesting
sections.html: Choice in GCAM is layered: sector → subsector → technology → (for thermal power) cooling system, each with its own logit (details_energy.html). The reference example uses γ = −3 between electricity subsectors and γ = −10 among coal technologies. In the kit's two-level nest (fossil nest with γ = −6 inside, then fossil vs solar with γ = −3) the result is coal 48.2%, gas 19.1%, solar 32.6%. Land and trade use logits too (Go 2.6).

callouts.title: Try it
callouts.html: Coal $60 and gas $70, γ = −2, equal weights. Coal's share? 60−2 = 2.78×10−4, 70−2 = 2.04×10−4, so coal = 2.78 / 4.82 = 58%.

callouts.title: In GCAM
callouts.html: Logit exponents are in gcamdata assumption files A21.subsector_logit.csv … A26.subsector_logit.csv; share-weight interpolation rules in A21.subsector_interp.csv and similar (inputs_supply.html). In XML they appear as <logit-exponent> and <share-weight> under each subsector and technology.

callouts.title: "A share weight is a subsidy"
callouts.html: No. A share weight is a calibrated preference multiplier with no money attached. Changing future share weights changes results without changing any cost, so state those assumptions openly.

explorer.intro: Set three costs and the logit exponent, and watch the market shares.
explorer.predict: Coal $60, gas $70, solar $80. Roughly what exponent gives coal 90% of the market?

code.title: Relative logit, calibration and a two-level nest
code.explain: Computes shares for three exponents, calibrates share weights to observed shares and builds a nest. Try: make solar $55 and predict whether it becomes the largest share at γ = −4.

takeaways: The logit turns costs into smooth shares: cheaper wins more, never everything
The exponent sets how sensitive shares are to cost differences
Share weights calibrate the base year and phase in new options; future values are assumptions
GCAM uses relative-cost and absolute-cost logits, nested from sector to technology
Example exponents: −3 between electricity fuels, −10 among coal technologies

quiz.q: In the absolute-cost logit, shares depend on…
quiz.explain: exp(β c) makes share ratios depend on c_i − c_j.

quiz.q: Which order matches GCAM's electricity nest?
quiz.explain: Sector, then fuel subsector, then technology, then cooling system.
